ncf00ad1d920.s: Which of the following pairs about Andhra Pradesh's Kharif 2026 season is correctly matched?
ncf00ad1d920.x: AP faced a 51 percent rainfall shortfall from 1 June to 25 August 2026 under El Niño conditions, so it proposed a water-budgeted shift towards pulses in Kharif 2026.

ndb0238b5bb9.s:
Consider the following statements about AP's fishing-ban relief for marine fishermen families:
1. YSR Matsyakara Bharosa raised the relief from Rs 4,000 to Rs 10,000 from 2019-20.
2. The relief was raised to Rs 20,000 per family from 2024-25.
3. The scheme was renamed Matsyakara Sevalo in 2019-20.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
ndb0238b5bb9.x: Relief rose to Rs 10,000 from 2019-20 and Rs 20,000 from 2024-25; the renaming as Matsyakara Sevalo came in 2025-26, not 2019-20.

n173f5e51be5.s: The Midlands industrial region is located in:
n173f5e51be5.x: The Midlands is an industrial region of England, not of the United States.

n9a89313cbd1.s: Cotton textile mills are not bound to raw-cotton sites because, in Weber's terms, raw cotton is a ____ material.
n9a89313cbd1.x: Raw cotton is non-weight-losing, so cotton textile mills are not necessarily tied to raw-cotton sites.

nworld-geography-33-11.s: Which industrial region – basis of growth pair is correctly matched?
o: Midlands – early Industrial Revolution, coal and iron ore
nworld-geography-33-11.x: The Midlands grew with the early Industrial Revolution, coal, iron ore and the canal and rail network.

nc89aab8243c.s: Which industrial region of India is described as an 'industrial workshop' for its textile, pharmaceutical and petrochemical industries?
nc89aab8243c.x: Coastal Gujarat is called an industrial workshop because of its textile, pharmaceutical and petrochemical industries.

n73641a3ff55.s: Vallarpadam, cited as an SEZ example, is located in which State?
n73641a3ff55.x: Vallarpadam is an SEZ example from Kerala; Nanguneri is the one from Tamil Nadu.

n44ca25ae996.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about National Investment and Manufacturing Zones (NIMZs)?
o: They follow exactly the same governance and fiscal rules as SEZs
They differ from SEZs in exit rules
n44ca25ae996.x: NIMZs differ from SEZs in governance, exit and fiscal rules, so saying they follow exactly the same rules is wrong.

new.s: In 2021-22, Andhra Pradesh ranked first in India in the production of:
new.x: AP was first in papaya (with oil palm, lime, coconut, cocoa, tomato and chillies); it was second in mango, cashew and sweet orange.

new.s: What is Andhra Pradesh's rank in India in mango production?
new.x: AP is second in mango production, not first; it is first in papaya, oil palm, cocoa and lime.

new.s: Which of the following crop – leading State pairs is wrongly matched?
new.x: Karnataka leads in silk; Andhra Pradesh is second.

new.s: Which district is a cashew hub of Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: Srikakulam, ASR and Parvathipuram-Manyam are the cashew hubs; Anantapur is a banana cluster and Chittoor a mango hub.

new.s: The banana cluster of Andhra Pradesh is centred on which district?
new.x: Banana is clustered in Anantapur and Rayalaseema.

new.s: Konaseema district is a horticulture hub for which crop?
new.x: Coconut hubs are East Godavari, Konaseema and Srikakulam.

new.s: Polavaram was declared a national project under which section of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
new.x: Section 90 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 declared Polavaram a national project.

new.s: The Pattiseema lift scheme links which two rivers?
new.x: Pattiseema lifts Godavari water into the Polavaram right main canal and releases it at Prakasam barrage on the Krishna.

new.s: The Veligonda (Poola Subbaiah) project, storing water in Nallamala Sagar, serves which district?
new.x: Veligonda carries Krishna floodwater from the Srisailam foreshore to Prakasam district.

new.s: How much Krishna floodwater does the Galeru-Nagari Sujala Sravanthi draw from the Srisailam foreshore?
new.x: Galeru-Nagari Sujala Sravanthi draws 38 TMC of Krishna floodwater for Rayalaseema.

new.s: The waters of the Vamsadhara project in Srikakulam are shared with which State?
new.x: The Vamsadhara waters are shared with Odisha.

new.s: How many agro-climatic zones does Andhra Pradesh have?
new.x: AP has 6 agro-climatic zones served by ANGRAU research stations.

new.s: The headquarters of ANGRAU, which serves AP's agro-climatic zones, is at:
new.x: ANGRAU is headquartered at Lam, Guntur; it shifted from Hyderabad in 2016.

new.s: The AP Integrated Irrigation and Agriculture Transformation Project (APIIATP) is funded by:
new.x: APIIATP is a World Bank project (US$ 172.2 million, 2018); APDMP is funded by IFAD.

new.s: AP's Gokul Gram cattle breeding farm under the Rashtriya Gokul Mission is at:
new.x: The Gokul Gram farm is at Chadalawada, Prakasam; Chintaladevi in Nellore hosts the National Kamdhenu Breeding Centre.

new.s: The National Kamdhenu Breeding Centre in Andhra Pradesh is located at:
new.x: The National Kamdhenu Breeding Centre is at Chintaladevi in Nellore district.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about native livestock breeds of Andhra Pradesh:
1. Punganur is a cattle breed.
2. Nellore is a sheep breed.
3. Aseel is a buffalo breed.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Ongole and Punganur are cattle, Nellore is sheep; Aseel is a poultry breed and Godavari the buffalo breed.

new.s: Tobacco in Andhra Pradesh is mainly grown in which districts?
new.x: Tobacco is a crop of Prakasam and Guntur; ASR (Araku) is the coffee area.

new.s: The Araku area of ASR district is known for which crop?
new.x: ASR (Araku) is the coffee area of AP, not a tobacco area.

new.s: Which provides the largest irrigated area in Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: Canals irrigate the most area in AP; tube wells lead only at the all-India level.

new.s: About how many minor irrigation tanks does Andhra Pradesh have?
new.x: AP's minor irrigation has 38,862 tanks with an ayacut of 25.60 lakh acres.

new.s: The total irrigation potential created in Andhra Pradesh up to December 2024 is:
new.x: Total potential created is 106.15 lakh acres; 66.81 is major, 25.60 is minor and 37.63 is the new potential of priority projects.

new.s: The cropping intensity of 1.88 in Andhra Pradesh relates to which year?
new.x: Cropping intensity was 1.88 in 2024-25; it was 1.21 in 2023-24.

new.s: After the 2023-24 remeasurement, Andhra Pradesh's 1,053 km coastline ranks ____ in India.
new.x: AP's coastline is now 1,053 km, the 3rd longest behind Gujarat and Tamil Nadu; earlier it was 974 km and 2nd.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh's fish production in 2024-25 was:
new.x: AP produced 55.39 LMT of fish in 2024-25; 51.58 LMT was 2023-24 and 51.06 LMT was 2022-23.

new.s: APSADA, which licenses aquaculture in Andhra Pradesh, was set up under:
o: AP State Aquaculture Development Authority Act, 2020
new.x: The AP State Aquaculture Development Authority Act, 2020 (Act 29 of 2020) set up APSADA.

new.s: Under the AP State Aquaculture Development Authority Act, 2020, aquaculture zones cover how many coastal districts?
new.x: Aquaculture zones are set in all 9 coastal districts.

new.s: Which of the following is a Phase I fishing harbour of Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: Machilipatnam (Krishna) is a Phase I harbour; Biyyaputhippa, Kothapatnam and Vodarevu are Phase II.

new.s: Which district produced 9.64 LMT of fish and shrimp worth ₹24,345 crore in 2025-26?
new.x: West Godavari produced 9.64 LMT of fish and shrimp worth ₹24,345 crore in 2025-26.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the PMMSY subsidy in Andhra Pradesh:
1. The general subsidy is 40 percent.
2. The Government of India bears 24 percent and the State 16 percent.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The PMMSY general subsidy is 40 percent, shared as 24 percent by GoI and 16 percent by GoAP.

new.s: In Weber's theory, the Material Index is the ratio of:
o: weight of finished product to weight of localised raw materials
weight of localised raw materials to weight of finished product
new.x: Material Index = weight of localised raw materials / weight of the finished product.

new.s: According to Weber, an industry with a Material Index greater than 1 locates:
new.x: MI > 1 means a weight-losing process, which pulls the industry to the raw material; MI < 1 pulls it to the market.

new.s: The substitution principle of industrial location is associated with:
new.x: Walter Isard gave the substitution principle, a trade-off between transport and other costs.

new.s: The maximum-profit or market-area approach to industrial location was given by:
new.x: August Losch gave the maximum-profit (market-area) approach; Weber gave least cost.

new.s: Which country led the world in shipbuilding new orders in 2025?
new.x: China was first (about 60-66 percent), South Korea second and Japan third.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about shipbuilding new orders in 2025:
1. China ranked first.
2. Japan ranked second.
3. South Korea held about 20 percent.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: China was first and South Korea second with about 20 percent; Japan was third, not second.

new.s: St. Petersburg is a well-known centre of which industry?
new.x: St. Petersburg, like Glasgow, Yokohama and Hamburg, is a shipbuilding centre.

new.s: Kemerovo is a centre of which industrial region?
new.x: Kemerovo lies in the Kuzbass (Kuznetsk Basin) of Siberia, not in the Donbas.

new.s: The Ruhr iron and steel industry obtained its iron ore from:
new.x: The Ruhr's iron ore came from Lorraine, not from the Ruhr itself.

new.s: The term 'Umland' was first used in:
new.x: Umland, the area around a town linked to it economically and culturally, was first used in 1883.

new.s: Which pair of cities is known for diamond cutting?
new.x: Amsterdam and Antwerp are the diamond-cutting centres.

new.s: Magnitogorsk and Chelyabinsk are iron and steel centres of which region?
new.x: Magnitogorsk and Chelyabinsk are in the Ural region of Russia.

new.s: Yawata is an iron and steel centre of which region?
new.x: Yawata is in the Kitakyushu region of Kyushu, Japan.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT among the main inputs needed to make steel?
new.x: About 4 tonnes of iron ore, coking coal, limestone and dolomite make 1 tonne of steel; bauxite is not among them.

new.s: The Flanders industrial region of Belgium is known for:
new.x: Flanders in Belgium is known for woollen and linen textiles.

new.s: Cuba is famous for which industry?
new.x: Cuba is known for cigars, not iron and steel.

new.s: China's share of world steel production is:
new.x: China is first in steel with over 50 percent of world output; India is second.

new.s: Muri in Jharkhand is known for which industry?
new.x: Muri (INDAL) and Renukoot (HINDALCO) are aluminium centres.

new.s: Koyali in Gujarat is known for:
new.x: Koyali is an oil-refinery centre.

new.s: Singrauli is called an 'energy enclave' because of its:
new.x: Singrauli is a coal and thermal power centre, the energy enclave.

new.s: Which of the following centre – industry pairs is wrongly matched?
new.x: Modinagar is a rubber centre; Aonla and Panki are the fertiliser centres.

new.s: The Hugli industrial region is chiefly known for which industry?
new.x: Hugli is the jute region; Rishra had the first jute mill in 1855.

new.s: The Kollam-Thiruvananthapuram industrial region is known for:
new.x: Kollam-Thiruvananthapuram is known for cashew, coir and rubber.

new.s: Pimpri and Nashik belong to which industrial region?
new.x: Mumbai-Pune includes Mumbai, Thane, Trombay, Pune, Pimpri, Nashik and Solapur.

new.s: Which one of the following is a minor industrial belt of India?
new.x: Durg-Raipur is a minor belt; Hugli, Mumbai-Pune and Chotanagpur are major industrial regions.

new.s: Which Five-Year Plan called for measures to attract industry to backward areas?
new.x: The Fourth Plan (1969-74) called for measures to attract industry to backward areas.

new.s: Which steel plants were placed away from raw-material bases for balanced regional growth?
new.x: Salem, Visakhapatnam and Vijayanagar steel plants were sited away from raw materials for regional balance.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956:
1. It sought balanced regional growth.
2. It placed public-sector units in backward regions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: IPR 1956 sought balanced regional growth and placed PSUs in backward regions.

new.s: The aluminium industry is primarily oriented towards:
new.x: Aluminium is power-oriented, needing 14,000-15,000 kWh per tonne.

new.s: The Amritsar-Kolkata Industrial Corridor (AKIC) is built on the:
new.x: AKIC uses the Eastern DFC; DMIC is built along the Western DFC.

new.s: How many national industrial corridors are there under NICDP?
new.x: There are 11 corridors under NICDP; 12 new industrial smart cities were approved in August 2024.

new.s: The Andhra Pradesh node of the Hyderabad-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor (HBIC) is:
new.x: HBIC's AP node is Orvakal in Kurnool; Krishnapatnam is the CBIC node.

new.s: The National Manufacturing Policy 2011, which introduced NIMZs, targeted a manufacturing share of GDP of:
new.x: The policy targeted manufacturing at 25 percent of GDP and 100 million jobs; manufacturing is now about 16-17 percent.
